Low resolution model of St. Lachtain's well in Freshford. The flower decorations were not there at my last few visits. A lady in the village told me that the water is supposed to heal sores. I would not recommend trying that, especially after the hedgehog has been floating in there for a while.

Wikidata: Q121840779

SMR no: KK013-025----

Made in KiriEngine from 156 images.
entries.title: Freshford: St Lachtain's Well (low poly)

entries.context: Found in the foundations of the chancel of St Mary's, Gowran (SMR KK020-060006-), demolished in 1827; the inscription was first noticed in 1849. Now on site in the rebuilt chancel. Described in OG(H)AM entry I-KIK-007.
entries.description: 3D model of the ogham stone from Gowran (Gabhrán), Co. Kilkenny, Ireland (CIIC 32; CISP GOWRN/1; SMR KK020-060007-), a grit pillar stone inscribed in Primitive Irish. It was found in the foundations of the chancel of the medieval parish church of St Mary's, Gowran, when the chancel was demolished in 1827, and is now displayed on site in the rebuilt chancel. The model was made with KIRI Engine from 111 photographs; the uploader notes that the scan is imperfect because of poor lighting on site.
entries.title: Gowran: Ogham Stone

entries.context: Found around 1851 in the ringfort at Garranes (SMR CO084-090001-), probably in its souterrain (SMR CO084-090002-); the findspot is recorded as SMR CO084-090003-. Probably acquired for the UCC collection in or around 1907. Now on permanent display in the Stone Corridor of University College Cork, Cork City (SMR CO074-148----, 51.8937, -8.4924), which is the present location, not the findspot. Described in OG(H)AM entry I-COR-030.
entries.description: 3D model of the ogham stone CIIC 81 (CISP GARES/1; University College Cork inv. no. 4), a green sandstone pillar inscribed in Primitive Irish with C[A]SSITT[A]S MAQI MU[CO]I CALLITI. It was unearthed around 1851 in the ringfort at Garranes (An Garrán), Co. Cork (SMR CO084-090003-), and is thought to have come from the souterrain there. Probably acquired for the UCC collection in or around 1907, it is now on permanent display in the Stone Corridor ('Rúin na gCloch / Stories in Stone') at University College Cork, Cork City (SMR CO074-148----).
entries.title: Cork Ogham Stone CIIC 81 (UCC 4)

entries.context: Self-built (own design, no commercial set) by Florian Thiery. Shown at the Apothekertrakt of Schönbrunn Palace during CHNT31, 2026-11-12 (https://www.openstreetmap.org/relation/6892072). The figure on top is read as a medieval warrior; that and any further identification are open hypotheses, not confirmed.
entries.description: Photogrammetric 3D scan (KIRI Engine) of a white stepped LEGO pyramid (nine levels) with a five-brick column and a minifigure-style warrior figure on top (spiked helmet, mail shirt, tunic, cloak), a hobby build by Florian Thiery; scanned on 2026-11-12 in the Apothekertrakt of Schönbrunn Palace, Vienna, where the model was on display during the CHNT31 conference. Raw scan without clean-up. The paired reconstruction is a separate FDOx and derives from this one.
entries.title: Lego Pyramid (KIRI Original)

entries.description: Idealised reconstruction of a white stepped LEGO pyramid (nine levels) with a five-brick column and a minifigure-style warrior figure on top (spiked helmet, mail shirt, tunic, cloak), a hobby build by Florian Thiery, rebuilt procedurally from clean LEGO bricks after a KIRI Engine scan. Only dimensions and structure were read from the scan; no scan mesh or texture was reused. AI disclosure: the reconstruction was generated with Claude (Anthropic, claude-sonnet-5-5) on behalf of Florian Thiery. It is an interpretation model, not a measurement.

entries.context: Early medieval sarcophagus from Govan Old (Govan Old Parish Church, Govan Road, Glasgow), rediscovered in the churchyard by a gravedigger in the mid-1850s (sources give 1855 and 1856); now displayed in the Govan Stones museum in the church. Numbered Govan 1 in the collection. The only sarcophagus of its kind recorded from pre-Norman northern Britain.
entries.description: 3D model of the Govan Sarcophagus (Govan 1), the best-known of the Govan Stones and a rare monument type in early medieval Scotland before the 12th century. Carved from solid sandstone, it is decorated with a hunting scene, differently arranged interlaced beasts and six panels of interlace, some of which appear to be interlaced snakes. It was rediscovered in the churchyard of Govan Old Parish Church in the mid-1850s and is now displayed in the Govan Stones museum there; how its lid looked is not known. The model was recorded by structure-from-motion photogrammetry for Megan N. Kasten's PhD research on the Govan Stones (University of Glasgow, 2019) and was published on Sketchfab by the Govan Stones account under CC BY 4.0.
entries.title: The Govan Sarcophagus (Govan 1, Govan Stones)

entries.context: Early medieval hogback grave monument from Govan Old (Govan Old Parish Church, Govan Road, Glasgow), where the five Govan hogbacks were found; now displayed in the Govan Stones museum in the church. Numbered Govan 2 by Stirling Maxwell and in the ECMS, Lang 1 in Lang's corpus. Smallest of the five hogbacks; Lang and Bailey suggest influences from Cumbria or further afield in its form and in the decoration along its lower edge.
entries.description: 3D model of Govan 2 (Stirling Maxwell and ECMS numbering; Lang 1), one of the five hogback grave monuments of Govan Old Parish Church in Glasgow. At about two metres in length it is the smallest of the five and the best preserved, and it is dated to the early 10th century. Above two rows of tegulation (roof-shingle carving) the 3D analysis shows what appears to be a row of step pattern along the worn ridge. The model was recorded by structure-from-motion photogrammetry as part of Megan N. Kasten's PhD research on the Govan Stones (University of Glasgow, 2019) and was published on Sketchfab by the Govan Stones account under CC BY 4.0.
entries.title: Govan 2 Hogback (Govan Stones)

entries.context: Found at Church Island (Oileán an Teampaill), Co. Kerry (SMR KE079-032004-), in a secondary position in the south-western quadrant of the island; now displayed in the Cork Public Museum, Cork (51.896085, -8.494222), inventory number 1777.1023 (G1094). Findspot and present location are different places; the spatial point of this FDO is the findspot. Described in OG(H)AM entry I-KER-136; CISP CHUIS/1; no CIIC number is listed.
entries.description: 3D model of the ogham stone CHUIS/1 (OG(H)AM I-KER-136; CISP CHUIS/1), a cross slab from Church Island (Oileán an Teampaill), Co. Kerry, now in the Cork Public Museum (inventory number 1777.1023, G1094). The slab measures 1.49 x 0.36 x 0.10 m and is fractured at its base. Its ogham inscription, read along the arris as BECCDINN MACI RIVVOESS, is in Primitive Irish, and a compass-drawn, incised ringed cross of Maltese type was added later; the excavator dates this design to 650-750 AD. The stone was found in a secondary position in the south-western quadrant of the island. The model was made with KIRI Engine from 77 photographs taken with a smartphone.
entries.title: Church Island Ogham Stone CHUIS/1 (Cork Public Museum)
